title: The New Lean Startup — Sid Bendre, Oleve
talk_summary: A founder of a 4-person, $6M-ARR consumer app portfolio describes operating principles (profit-first, KPI ownership, continuous process refinement, 'don't learn it twice' blueprints) and a harvester/cultivator org model, plus a three-stage AI augmentation ladder from human-led tooling to workflow automation to multi-agent orchestration. The concrete, copyable mechanisms are limited: using a feature-flag service as an LLM traffic router/load balancer and as an on-the-fly reordering layer for flaky third-party ingestion waterfalls, and investing in reusable blueprints/templates.

takeaways.technique: Feature-flag layer as LLM traffic router
takeaways.what_they_do: They put LaunchDarkly between all LLM calls so traffic can be rerouted to different providers on the fly when hitting rate limits or for strategic reasons, splitting load within quotas.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we put Launch Sharkly in between all our LM calls so that we can reroute traffic to different LM providers based on hitting rate limits

takeaways.technique: Flag-controlled reordering of flaky dependency waterfalls
takeaways.what_they_do: For file ingestion that depends on multiple unreliable third-party services, they use flags to change the prioritization/order of the waterfall on the fly when a service goes down.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if one of these third party thirdarty services goes down, we're able to reorganize the service on the fly to make sure it's up and running

takeaways.what_they_do: They invest in code-complete templates, internal libraries, and shared infrastructure (notifications, experimentation layer) built as a first layer into every new product, so new products launch faster.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It took 3 weeks to build thanks to all the blueprints that we've built in advance
takeaways.numbers: third product built in 3 weeks; Unstuck hit 1M users in under 9 weeks

takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately sequence automation: first embed tools in human workflows, then hand whole workflows to automation, then consolidate workflows under one multi-agent orchestration serving as one 'employee'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: consolidating all the workflows that we've built under one autonomous decision-making system, i.e. an orchestration of multiple agents working together

takeaways.technique: Failures treated as systems failures with per-run retrospective
takeaways.what_they_do: For every repeating process they ask what went wrong in the previous run and treat issues as system failures, creating a feedback loop for process improvement.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We view failures in the company and issues in the company as systems failures, which lets us set up a feedback loop
